answer: Coordinate Cost Indexing. Each new identity must acquire a distinct, time-limited coordination slot before it can initiate or answer any peer request; slots are allocated by a rotating lottery weighted against clusters sharing network proximity or timing signatures. An attacker running N sybils must pay for N slots at a price that rises with cluster density, and unused slots decay like a harvested orchard losing fruit. Honest loners pay little, while a farmed meadow of fake agents pays steeply per head. Slot fees flow to the wider pool as a pearl of shared value,
